The 15 holdings and how they did

Weight from Goal Programming (2% to 15%). Score is the Integer Programming selection score. Return, volatility, Sharpe, beta and drawdown are training-window values; the last two columns are the test year. Contribution = weight × test-year return.

Behavioural clusters this year

Cluster numbers are arbitrary; the description names features at least half a standard deviation from the window average.

Choosing K

Silhouette score per candidate K. K is the best-scoring value that lets the selection take 15 stocks with at most 3 per cluster from at least 5 clusters; faded bars cannot.

Proposed minus each baseline, per test year

Dot is the mean yearly difference, line its bootstrap 95% interval. Right of zero favours the proposed portfolio. Computed with 0.25% costs.

Paired comparison table

Wins = test years where the proposed portfolio was better. p is the Wilcoxon signed-rank test on the yearly differences. For drawdown a positive difference means the proposed portfolio fell less.

Market regimes

Average test-year Sharpe ratio. A year is Bull if the NIFTY 50 rose, and high-volatility if its volatility was above the median test year. Labels are set after the fact and never used to build portfolios.

Sharpe ratio when one design choice changes

Each bar is a full re-run of all 22 years with a single change. The dashed line is the NIFTY 50. Computed with 0.25% costs. These runs test sensitivity; none was used to pick the primary model.

Experiment details

Shared holdings = average share of each year's 15 stocks that the primary model also held.
